newsitem.title: USA: U.S. talk show host Sonny Bloch gets prison term.
newsitem.headline: U.S. talk show host Sonny Bloch gets prison term.

text.p: Sonny Bloch, who had been host of one of the nation's longest-running financial talks shows, was sentenced on Thursday to 21 months in prison for personal and corporate income tax evasion and lying to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Bloch, who previously pleaded to a total of seven counts, was also sentenced to three years of probation during which he will provide 750 hours of community service.
During his plea, Bloch admitted failing to report $263,406 in personal income tax for calendar 1991, 1992 and 1993.

He also said he aided Broadcast Mangement Corp, which produced his radio program, with filing false returns for the same years and evading $146,771. He said he lied to the SEC in 1994 about the income tax returns.

U.S. District Judge Shira Scheindlin said she was not imposing a fine because of other financial claims against him, including $3.9 million by the Securities and Exchange Commission and $410,000 by the Internal Revenue Service.
